```plato
    //==
    // # Marching squares — the case table
    //
    // One row of four entries per configuration: up to two segments, each a pair
    // of edge indices, terminated by -1. Row c begins at c * 4. A segment runs
    // from its first edge to its second so that the extracted region — the
    // at-or-above side — lies to its LEFT, matching the counter-clockwise-outside
    // winding the tree uses everywhere else.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding.
    //
    // Cases 5 and 10 are the saddles, where all four edges are cut and the two
    // pairings are equally consistent with the corner values. They are resolved
    // SEPARATED: each cut corner gets its own segment, so the two at-or-above
    // corners of case 5 are disjoint rather than joined through the middle. The
    // alternative needs the center sample the cell does not have.
    //
    // Dispatched on `Line2D` — the type the extraction produces — following the
    // tree's constant idiom, and read as `Line2D.MarchingSquaresCaseTable`. Build
    // it ONCE per extraction and pass it down: an array literal allocates on every
    // evaluation.
    MarchingSquaresCaseTable(_: Line2D): Array<Integer>
        => [
            -1, -1, -1, -1,
             3,  0, -1, -1,
             0,  1, -1, -1,
             3,  1, -1, -1,
             1,  2, -1, -1,
             1,  0,  3,  2,
             0,  2, -1, -1,
             3,  2, -1, -1,
             2,  3, -1, -1,
             2,  0, -1, -1,
             0,  3,  2,  1,
             2,  1, -1, -1,
             1,  3, -1, -1,
             1,  0, -1, -1,
             0,  3, -1, -1,
            -1, -1, -1, -1,
        ];
```
